description:
Split from af4c901a integration: default-rule MEMBERSHIP is reconciled from the config registry in memory at load, but .jit/rules.toml entries are not updated, so the addressable rule registry (@/rule/<name> resolves rules.toml entries) can lag effective membership. Observed live: brackets was declared unique after scaffold; reconciliation enforced namespace-unique-brackets and the rules-and-gates projection documented it, while @/rule/namespace-unique-brackets dangled until the entry was added by hand.

## Background

The refresh path from af4c901a already republishes schemas/default-*.json on jit-driven config writes. Extending it to append/drop default-origin namespace-unique-* rule ENTRIES in rules.toml on the same trigger keeps the addressable registry consistent with derived membership. Custom rules and default-rule policy fields (severity, enforce, selector) stay untouched.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A jit-driven write that changes the config namespace registry appends the namespace-unique-* entry for a newly-unique namespace to rules.toml and drops the entry for a namespace no longer unique or removed, for origin=default entries only. Add-only syncs preserve all other file content byte-exact; a membership drop may canonicalize TOML syntax decoration elsewhere in the file (semantically lossless re-serialization, invoker-approved 2026-07-17) and preserves all other content semantically intact.
- [hard] REQ-02: Rule addressability (@/rule/<name>) resolves every effectively-enforced default rule after such a write; docs-mechanical citation checking cannot dangle on a reconciled rule.
- [hard] REQ-03: Hand edits to default-rule policy fields and all custom rules survive the rewrite; tests cover append, drop, and preservation.
- Out of scope: changing in-memory reconciliation semantics (they remain authoritative at load).
title: Write default-rule membership through to rules.toml on config-driven refresh
